views.name: batting_season_player_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  year,
  SUM(COALESCE(g,0)) AS g,
  SUM(COALESCE(ab,0)) AS ab,
  SUM(COALESCE(r,0)) AS r,
  SUM(COALESCE(h,0)) AS h,
  SUM(COALESCE("double",0)) AS "double",
  SUM(COALESCE(triple,0)) AS triple,
  SUM(COALESCE(hr,0)) AS hr,
  SUM(COALESCE(rbi,0)) AS rbi,
  SUM(COALESCE(sb,0)) AS sb,
  SUM(COALESCE(cs,0)) AS cs,
  SUM(COALESCE(bb,0)) AS bb,
  SUM(COALESCE(so,0)) AS so
FROM batting
GROUP BY player_id, year

params.description: Season-level batting totals per player (one row per player_id and year) summarizing counting stats aggregated from the batting table.
params.when_to_use: Get season totals for a given player and year (e.g., how many hits, home runs, walks a player had in a season). | Compare players' counting-stat totals within a season or across seasons (e.g., list top players by hits in 2019). | Compose rate or ratio metrics (e.g., batting average, OPS) by joining these season totals with derived or contextual tables. | Join to player or team dimension data to produce enriched season reports (player name, team, franchise) without needing to re-aggregate batting events.
params.output_schema: player_id: identifier for the player; sourced from batting.player_id (grouping key). | year: season year; sourced from batting.year (grouping key). | g: games — SUM(COALESCE(batting.g, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | ab: at bats — SUM(COALESCE(batting.ab, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | r: runs — SUM(COALESCE(batting.r, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | h: hits — SUM(COALESCE(batting.h, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | double: doubles — SUM(COALESCE(batting."double", 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | triple: triples — SUM(COALESCE(batting.triple, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | hr: home runs — SUM(COALESCE(batting.hr, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | rbi: runs batted in — SUM(COALESCE(batting.rbi, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | sb: stolen bases — SUM(COALESCE(batting.sb, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | cs: caught stealing — SUM(COALESCE(batting.cs, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | bb: base on balls (walks) — SUM(COALESCE(batting.bb, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group. | so: strikeouts — SUM(COALESCE(batting.so, 0)) aggregated over batting rows for the (player_id, year) group.
params.grounded_columns: batting.player_id | batting.year | batting.g | batting.ab | batting.r | batting.h | batting."double" | batting.triple | batting.hr | batting.rbi | batting.sb | batting.cs | batting.bb | batting.so
params.metric: g = SUM(COALESCE(batting.g, 0)) | ab = SUM(COALESCE(batting.ab, 0)) | r = SUM(COALESCE(batting.r, 0)) | h = SUM(COALESCE(batting.h, 0)) | double = SUM(COALESCE(batting."double", 0)) | triple = SUM(COALESCE(batting.triple, 0)) | hr = SUM(COALESCE(batting.hr, 0)) | rbi = SUM(COALESCE(batting.rbi, 0)) | sb = SUM(COALESCE(batting.sb, 0)) | cs = SUM(COALESCE(batting.cs, 0)) | bb = SUM(COALESCE(batting.bb, 0)) | so = SUM(COALESCE(batting.so, 0))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_core.player_id = batting_season_player_agg.player_id — safe because player_core is a normalized player dimension (one row per player) so joining will not duplicate batting measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_season_summary on (team_season_summary.year = batting_season_player_agg.year AND team_season_summary.team_id = <derived team_id if available>) — only safe if you first resolve a single team_id per (player_id, year). If player-team relationship is many-to-one for the season and you have a single team_id per player-season, joining to team_season_summary will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_season_rank_by_hits or player_season_above_threshold_cohort on (player_id, year) — safe because those sibling views are expected to be at the same grain (player_id, year) or filtered selections/ ranks per player-season. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example, detailed batting events, awards list with multiple rows per player-season, or salary_player_year if it contains multiple salary rows per player-year) without re-aggregation or ensuring uniqueness first — such joins will multiply the aggregated counts in this view because batting_season_player_agg is aggregated to player_id/year and a many-row match will duplicate its measures. | If you need to join to a one-to-many relation (e.g., player_awards_summary may have multiple awards rows per player-season), either: (a) aggregate that relation to one row per player_id/year before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate across player_id/year to restore correct totals. Failure to do so will overcount g, ab, h, etc. | When composing rate metrics (e.g., batting average = h / ab), compute them after any joins that might change the denominator, and prefer calculating rates from these aggregated columns (h and ab) to preserve numeric correctness and avoid division by zero (check ab > 0).

views.description: Season-level batting aggregates per player (summed across stints and teams). Useful for player-season leaderboards, rate calculations (AVG, SLG when combined with extra-base breakdowns), and joins to player or team-season records. | Use for: Who led the league in hits/HR/RBI in a given season (after joining to player or team)?; Compute batting averages (h/ab) or rates for players by season; List players with at least N plate appearances (needs ab + bb/hbp if extended)

views.name: pitching_season_player_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  year,
  SUM(COALESCE(w,0)) AS w,
  SUM(COALESCE(l,0)) AS l,
  SUM(COALESCE(g,0)) AS g,
  SUM(COALESCE(gs,0)) AS gs,
  SUM(COALESCE(cg,0)) AS cg,
  SUM(COALESCE(sho,0)) AS sho,
  SUM(COALESCE(sv,0)) AS sv,
  SUM(COALESCE(ipouts,0)) AS ipouts,
  SUM(COALESCE(h,0)) AS h,
  SUM(COALESCE(er,0)) AS er,
  SUM(COALESCE(hr,0)) AS hr,
  SUM(COALESCE(bb,0)) AS bb,
  SUM(COALESCE(so,0)) AS so
FROM pitching
GROUP BY player_id, year

params.description: Season-level pitching totals per player: aggregate counting/accumulation of pitching statistics for each player in a given year.
params.when_to_use: Get season totals for a given player and year (e.g., total wins, losses, innings outs, strikeouts in 1998 for player X). | Build rate metrics at the player-season grain (e.g., ERA, K/9) by composing with this view's aggregated counts. | Rank or filter players based on season pitching volume or counting stats (e.g., find players with >= 100 innings outs or >= 100 strikeouts in a year). | Join to player or team dimension records to add descriptive attributes without duplicating pitching measures (one-to-one joins). | Use as the aggregated input when combining with other event/detail tables — re-aggregate after joining any table that is one-to-many to avoid double-counting.
params.output_schema: player_id: unique identifier of the player for whom season totals are produced; sourced from pitching.player_id. | year: season year corresponding to these aggregated pitching totals; sourced from pitching.year. | w: total wins in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.w, 0)). | l: total losses in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.l, 0)). | g: total games pitched in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.g, 0)). | gs: total games started in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.gs, 0)). | cg: total complete games in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.cg, 0)). | sho: total shutouts in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.sho, 0)). | sv: total saves in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.sv, 0)). | ipouts: total outs recorded (thirds of innings as outs) in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.ipouts, 0)). | h: total hits allowed in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.h, 0)). | er: total earned runs allowed in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.er, 0)). | hr: total home runs allowed in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.hr, 0)). | bb: total base on balls (walks) allowed in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.bb, 0)). | so: total strikeouts in that season for the player; derived as SUM(COALESCE(pitching.so, 0)).
params.grounded_columns: pitching.player_id | pitching.year | pitching.w | pitching.l | pitching.g | pitching.gs | pitching.cg | pitching.sho | pitching.sv | pitching.ipouts | pitching.h | pitching.er | pitching.hr | pitching.bb | pitching.so
params.metric: w = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.w, 0)) | l = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.l, 0)) | g = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.g, 0)) | gs = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.gs, 0)) | cg = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.cg, 0)) | sho = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.sho, 0)) | sv = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.sv, 0)) | ipouts = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.ipouts, 0)) | h = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.h, 0)) | er = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.er, 0)) | hr = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.hr, 0)) | bb = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.bb, 0)) | so = SUM(COALESCE(pitching.so, 0))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_id — safe because player_core is one row per player (or one canonical row per player_id) so joining adds attributes without duplicating these season totals. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_season_summary on (team_id, year) only after ensuring a one-to-one relationship between this view's rows and the team key (this view is per player-year; if you first map player-year to a single team_id for that year, the join will not duplicate aggregates). | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many detail tables (for example: per-appearance, per-game, or event-level tables derived from pitching rows) without re-aggregation, because such joins will multiply rows and double-count the measures. If you need to augment with one-to-many detail data, either: |   - aggregate the detail table to player_id+year first (same grain) and then join on (player_id, year), or |   - join the detail and then re-aggregate the combined result grouped by (player_id, year) to recompute correct totals. | do NOT join to sibling aggregate views that are at a finer grain (e.g., individual pitching appearances) unless those sibling views are pre-aggregated to player_id+year. Joining to other player-season aggregates (like batting_season_player_agg) on (player_id, year) is safe because they share the same grain. | When composing rate metrics (e.g., ERA = 9 * er / (ipouts/3)), compute them using these summed columns so the numerator and denominator are from the same aggregation; avoid computing rates by joining this view to per-game data and dividing without re-aggregation.

views.description: Season-level pitching aggregates per player (summed across stints and teams). Useful for leaderboards (wins, strikeouts), rate metrics (ERA needs ipouts/3 but can be joined), and joining to player or team-season data. | Use for: Who had the most strikeouts/wins in a season?; Compute season ERA approximations (need ipouts->innings) or WHIP when combined with walks; Filter pitchers by workload (games, ipouts) for leaderboards

views.name: team_season_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  league_id,
  team_id,
  franchise_id,
  div_id,
  rank,
  g,
  w,
  l,
  r,
  ab,
  h,
  "double",
  triple,
  hr,
  bb,
  so,
  sb,
  cs,
  era,
  name,
  park,
  team_id_br,
  team_id_lahman45,
  team_id_retro
FROM team

params.description: Season-level summary of team statistics and identifiers (one row per team per year).
params.when_to_use: Get team-level season totals and identifiers for a given year or range of years. | Join team season-level metrics into player- or franchise-level analyses after ensuring correct aggregation. | Create league- or division-level aggregations from team-season rows (e.g., league runs per year) by summing appropriate measures. | Filter or look up team metadata (name, park, cross-referenced team IDs) for a specific team-season.
params.output_schema: year: Season year (team.year) | league_id: League identifier for the season (team.league_id) | team_id: Primary team identifier for the season (team.team_id) | franchise_id: Franchise identifier associated with the team (team.franchise_id) | div_id: Division identifier for the season (team.div_id) | rank: Team rank/standing in the season (team.rank) | g: Games played by the team in the season (team.g) | w: Wins for the team in the season (team.w) | l: Losses for the team in the season (team.l) | r: Runs scored by the team in the season (team.r) | ab: Team at-bats in the season (team.ab) | h: Team hits in the season (team.h) | double: Team doubles in the season (team."double") | triple: Team triples in the season (team.triple) | hr: Team home runs in the season (team.hr) | bb: Team walks (bases on balls) in the season (team.bb) | so: Team strikeouts in the season (team.so) | sb: Team stolen bases in the season (team.sb) | cs: Team caught stealing in the season (team.cs) | era: Team earned run average for the season (team.era) | name: Team name for the season (team.name) | park: Home park identifier/name for the season (team.park) | team_id_br: Baseball-Reference team id for the season (team.team_id_br) | team_id_lahman45: Lahman45 team id for the season (team.team_id_lahman45) | team_id_retro: Retrosheet/Retro IDs for the team-season (team.team_id_retro)
params.grounded_columns: team.year | team.league_id | team.team_id | team.franchise_id | team.div_id | team.rank | team.g | team.w | team.l | team.r | team.ab | team.h | team."double" | team.triple | team.hr | team.bb | team.so | team.sb | team.cs | team.era | team.name | team.park | team.team_id_br | team.team_id_lahman45 | team.team_id_retro
params.metric: g = team.g  -- raw column representing games played (no further aggregation inside this view) | w = team.w  -- raw column wins | l = team.l  -- raw column losses | r = team.r  -- raw column runs scored | ab = team.ab  -- raw column at-bats | h = team.h  -- raw column hits | double = team."double"  -- raw column doubles | triple = team.triple  -- raw column triples | hr = team.hr  -- raw column home runs | bb = team.bb  -- raw column walks | so = team.so  -- raw column strikeouts | sb = team.sb  -- raw column stolen bases | cs = team.cs  -- raw column caught stealing | era = team.era  -- raw column earned run average (already a per-team-season rate in source) | rank = team.rank  -- standings rank (source-provided) | name = team.name  -- team display name | park = team.park  -- home park identifier/name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_franchise_active on franchise_id AND year — safe because team_season_summary has at most one row per (year, team_id) and team_franchise_active is a selector of franchise-level state (one row per franchise per relevant key). The join will not duplicate team-season measures if the franchise view is 1:1 or 1:0 for the franchise per year. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to park_reference on park (or park + year if park_reference is year-partitioned) — safe when park_reference is one-row-per-park (or one-row-per park-year). This will not multiply team metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core when linking via team_id/team-season only after aggregating player rows to team-season (e.g., summing player metrics grouped by year, team_id). Do NOT directly join player_core (one-to-many players per team-season) without pre-aggregation, because that would duplicate team-level measures. | do NOT join directly to batting_season_player_agg or pitching_season_player_agg without aggregating those player-season rows up to team-season on (year, team_id) first. Those sibling views are many-player rows per team-season and will multiply team-level measures if joined directly. | do NOT join team_season_summary to any raw event-level or player-season detail (e.g., player_awards_summary, salary_player_year) without first ensuring those sources are aggregated to the same grain (year, team_id) or joined in a way that preserves cardinality (e.g., use SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY year, team_id) or pre-aggregate). | safe aggregation patterns: to create league-level metrics from this view, SUM numeric columns (r, ab, h, hr, bb, etc.) grouped by year and league_id — safe because team_season_summary is already at team-season grain and will not double-count when summed across teams. | key recommendations for planners: treat team_season_summary as canonical at-grain (year, team_id). Any join target that is one-row-per-(year, team_id) or one-row-per-team (static lookup) is safe. Any one-to-many target per team-season must be reduced (aggregated or limited) before joining to avoid multiplication of measures.

views.description: Canonical team-season summary (one row per team in a given year) projecting core measures and identifiers. Useful as the team-side for joins to player-season aggregates, franchise analysis, and season-level comparisons. | Use for: Compare team offensive/defensive totals across seasons; Join with batting_season_player_agg or pitching_season_player_agg to allocate player contributions to team seasons; Filter teams by rank, wins, or playoff wins

views.name: player_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  birth_year,
  birth_month,
  birth_day,
  birth_country,
  birth_state,
  birth_city,
  death_year,
  death_month,
  death_day,
  death_country,
  death_state,
  death_city,
  name_first,
  name_last,
  name_given,
  weight,
  height,
  bats,
  throws,
  debut,
  final_game,
  retro_id,
  bbref_id
FROM player

params.description: Canonical one-row-per-player core demographic and identifier attributes for baseball players.
params.when_to_use: Look up player demographic details (birth/death dates and places, physical attributes) by player_id or name. | Enrich season- or game-level aggregates with stable player attributes (e.g., weight, height, batting/throwing handedness, debut/final dates). | Join player identifiers (retro_id, bbref_id) to map between identifier spaces. | Filter or cohort players by birth/death attributes or debut/final_game dates before composing performance aggregates.
params.output_schema: player_id: Unique player identifier (player.player_id). Grain: one row per player. | birth_year: Player birth year (player.birth_year). | birth_month: Player birth month (player.birth_month). | birth_day: Player birth day of month (player.birth_day). | birth_country: Player birth country (player.birth_country). | birth_state: Player birth state/province (player.birth_state). | birth_city: Player birth city (player.birth_city). | death_year: Player death year (player.death_year). | death_month: Player death month (player.death_month). | death_day: Player death day of month (player.death_day). | death_country: Player death country (player.death_country). | death_state: Player death state/province (player.death_state). | death_city: Player death city (player.death_city). | name_first: Player first name (player.name_first). | name_last: Player last name / family name (player.name_last). | name_given: Player full given name(s) (player.name_given). | weight: Player weight in pounds (player.weight). | height: Player height in inches (player.height). | bats: Batting handedness (player.bats). | throws: Throwing handedness (player.throws). | debut: Player MLB debut date (player.debut). | final_game: Player last MLB game date (player.final_game). | retro_id: Retrosheet identifier for player (player.retro_id). | bbref_id: Baseball-Reference identifier for player (player.bbref_id).
params.grounded_columns: player.player_id | player.birth_year | player.birth_month | player.birth_day | player.birth_country | player.birth_state | player.birth_city | player.death_year | player.death_month | player.death_day | player.death_country | player.death_state | player.death_city | player.name_first | player.name_last | player.name_given | player.weight | player.height | player.bats | player.throws | player.debut | player.final_game | player.retro_id | player.bbref_id
params.metric: This view exposes no derived aggregates or computed metrics; all columns are pass-through attributes from the player table. Example: height = player.height (no aggregation).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to season- or game-level aggregated views on player_id (e.g., batting_season_player_agg.player_id, pitching_season_player_agg.player_id, player_season_above_threshold_cohort.player_id, player_season_rank_by_hits.player_id, player_awards_summary.player_id, salary_player_year.player_id) — safe because player_core has exactly one row per player_id, so joining it to an aggregation that is one-row-per-(player_id, season) will not duplicate the player-level attributes; measures in the aggregation remain correct. | Safe join example: batting_season_player_agg JOIN player_core ON batting_season_player_agg.player_id = player_core.player_id — batting aggregates stay at their season granularity. | Do NOT join player_core to one-to-many child tables (e.g., raw events, play-by-play, or any unaggregated per-game/per-plate-appearance table) expecting to preserve counts or aggregates present only on player_core — joining player_core (1 row) to a one-to-many table (many rows) will multiply the other table's rows but will not duplicate player_core rows; however, if you instead start from player_core and join to a one-to-many table to produce aggregated measures you must re-aggregate after the join to avoid mistaken cardinality assumptions. | If you need to combine player attributes with other one-to-many facts and keep player-level measures constant, aggregate the many-side first (e.g., SUM/COUNT by player_id) and then join the resulting one-row-per-player aggregation to player_core. | Joining to team_franchise_active or park_reference: join on shared keys only if those views have matching cardinality semantics. For example, do not assume player_core can be safely joined directly to team_franchise_active without confirming the join key (player_id is not a team key); join player_core to team-level data only when there is a player_id linkage (e.g., roster or season-player table) and ensure the team-side is pre-aggregated to the desired grain. | Identifier joins: joining to salary_player_year on player_id is safe when salary_player_year is at player-year grain (one or few rows per player-year) — composition will preserve salary rows while enriching them with player attributes.

views.description: Canonical player reference rows with personal attributes and birth/death details. Use for joins to attach human-readable names and demographic attributes to stats. | Use for: Lookup player biographical info for display alongside stats; Filter players by birth_country/state or debut/final_game ranges; Resolve name-based searches before joining to stats

views.name: player_season_above_threshold_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  year,
  g,
  ab,
  r,
  h,
  "double",
  triple,
  hr,
  rbi,
  sb,
  cs,
  bb,
  so
FROM batting_season_player_agg

params.description: Season-level batting totals per player (one row per player_id + year) suitable for answering batting-count questions and for composing aggregate summaries by player or year.
params.when_to_use: Get a player's batting totals in a specific year (e.g., how many games, hits, HRs did player X have in 2019). | Compare per-player seasonal counting statistics across players for the same year (e.g., rank players by hits or HR in a given season). | Compose higher-level aggregates (team- or league-season totals) by summing these player-season rows. | Filter players who exceed thresholds in seasonal counting stats (e.g., players above a minimum AB or H) before joining to other dimension tables.
params.output_schema: player_id: player identifier — directly selected from batting_season_player_agg.player_id | year: season year — directly selected from batting_season_player_agg.year | g: games played (count of games for that player in that season) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.g | ab: at-bats (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.ab | r: runs scored (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.r | h: hits (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.h | double: doubles (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg."double" | triple: triples (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.triple | hr: home runs (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.hr | rbi: runs batted in (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.rbi | sb: stolen bases (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.sb | cs: caught stealing (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.cs | bb: bases on balls / walks (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.bb | so: strikeouts (count) — sourced from batting_season_player_agg.so
params.grounded_columns: batting_season_player_agg.player_id | batting_season_player_agg.year | batting_season_player_agg.g | batting_season_player_agg.ab | batting_season_player_agg.r | batting_season_player_agg.h | batting_season_player_agg."double" | batting_season_player_agg.triple | batting_season_player_agg.hr | batting_season_player_agg.rbi | batting_season_player_agg.sb | batting_season_player_agg.cs | batting_season_player_agg.bb | batting_season_player_agg.so
params.metric: g = batting_season_player_agg.g | ab = batting_season_player_agg.ab | r = batting_season_player_agg.r | h = batting_season_player_agg.h | double = batting_season_player_agg."double" | triple = batting_season_player_agg.triple | hr = batting_season_player_agg.hr | rbi = batting_season_player_agg.rbi | sb = batting_season_player_agg.sb | cs = batting_season_player_agg.cs | bb = batting_season_player_agg.bb | so = batting_season_player_agg.so
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_id — safe because player_core is one row per player (normalized player entity), so joining retains one row per player-season and does NOT duplicate the batting measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_season_summary on year (and team key if batting_season_player_agg contained team — note: this view does not expose team, so join only on year) — only safe when aggregating this view by year to match the team-season grain; direct join by year will not duplicate measures if you aggregate appropriately (e.g., sum player metrics grouped by year before joining to a single team-season row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_awards_summary on (player_id, year) — safe when player_awards_summary is one-row-per-player-year; it will not duplicate batting measures because both are at player+year grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_season_rank_by_hits on (player_id, year) — safe because that ranking view is at the same player+year grain. | unsafe to join without care: do NOT join directly to salary_player_year (if salary_player_year is one-to-many per player+year) without ensuring salary is aggregated to one row per player+year first — otherwise player-season batting counts will be multiplied by salary-side rows. | unsafe to join without care: do NOT join directly to player_awards_summary or any award/transaction table if those sibling tables contain multiple rows per player+year (e.g., one row per award or transaction) unless you first reduce them to one row per player+year (e.g., aggregate or choose a single row) because such joins would duplicate batting counts. | unsafe to join without care: do NOT join to team_franchise_active or park_reference if those tables are at a different grain (e.g., multiple parks per team-season) without aggregating/joining on keys that ensure one-to-one correspondence — duplications happen when the join side has multiple rows per player+year. | general planner guidance: this view's grain is exactly (player_id, year). Any join to another table/view is safe (i.e., will not duplicate the counting metrics) only when the other side is guaranteed to be at the same grain (player_id, year) or at a strictly higher/coarser grain and you first aggregate this view to that coarser grain (for example, summing metrics over players to produce year-level totals). If the other side is one-to-many relative to (player_id, year), reduce/aggregate that side to one row per player+year before joining.

views.description: Selectable cohort of player-season rows from batting_season_player_agg that meet an activity threshold (exposes ab and h for downstream rate calc). Keeps threshold out of the CTE; use WHERE when consuming. Useful for filtering to regular players (e.g., minimum plate appearances) before ranking. | Use for: Identify qualified batters for leaderboards (consumer will add WHERE ab>=some_value); Compute batting averages or slugging for a filtered cohort

views.name: player_season_rank_by_hits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  year,
  h,
  ab,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY COALESCE(h,0) DESC, player_id ASC) AS hits_rank
FROM batting_season_player_agg

params.description: Ranks players by hits within each season (year), returning one row per player-season with hits, at-bats, and the hit rank within that year.
params.when_to_use: Find a player's rank by hits for a given year | List top-N players by hits in a season | Compose season-level leaderboards or comparisons using hits rank | Join to player or team dimensions to display rank alongside player/team attributes
params.output_schema: player_id: unique identifier of the player for the season — derived directly from batting_season_player_agg.player_id | year: season year — derived directly from batting_season_player_agg.year | h: total hits for the player in that season — derived directly from batting_season_player_agg.h | ab: total at-bats for the player in that season — derived directly from batting_season_player_agg.ab | hits_rank: 1-based rank of the player within the same year ordered by hits descending (ties broken by player_id ascending) — computed using ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY COALESCE(h,0) DESC, player_id ASC)
params.metric: h = batting_season_player_agg.h | ab = batting_season_player_agg.ab | hits_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batting_season_player_agg.year ORDER BY COALESCE(batting_season_player_agg.h, 0) DESC, batting_season_player_agg.player_id ASC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_id — safe because player_core is one-row-per-player (normal dimension); joining will not duplicate this view's player-season measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_franchise_active on franchise_id or team key (if you first join batting_season_player_agg -> team key) only if that join is one-to-one per season-player; verify team key is unique per player-season before joining to avoid duplication. | do NOT join directly to batting_season_player_agg (or other one-to-many event/detail tables) again without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply rows/measures because this view is already at the player-season grain (player_id, year). If you need event-level detail, aggregate the detail to player-season first and then join. | do NOT join to player_awards_summary or salary_player_year or other tables that may have multiple rows per player-season without ensuring a one-row-per(player_id,year) result from those tables (e.g., aggregate or pick a single row) — otherwise hits_rank and the h/ab measures will be duplicated. | safe composition pattern: to compute combined metrics (e.g., hits per award), first reduce the other sibling view to player_id+year (one row) via aggregation or filtering (e.g., SUM, MAX, or ROW_NUMBER + filter), then join to this view on (player_id, year). This preserves the one-row-per-player-season cardinality and avoids multiplying hits/ab/hits_rank.

views.description: Season-level rank of players by hits within each year. Exposes a rank column so callers can filter for Top-K per season by applying WHERE hits_rank <= K. Useful for year-by-year leaderboards and tie-aware ranking. | Use for: Top K hitters by hits per season (apply WHERE hits_rank <= K); Compare ranking positions across seasons

views.name: team_franchise_active
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  franchise_id,
  franchise_name,
  active,
  na_assoc
FROM team_franchise

params.description: One-row-per-franchise lookup of franchise identity and current active / NA-association flags from the team_franchise table.
params.when_to_use: Return franchise name and simple boolean flags (active, na_assoc) for a given franchise_id or list of franchise_ids. | Join franchise descriptive flags onto franchise-level aggregates (e.g., team or season summaries) without changing cardinality. | Filter or group by whether a franchise is active or NA-associated when composing larger queries (for reporting, filtering cohorts, or labeling results).
params.output_schema: franchise_id: Franchise identifier – derives from team_franchise.franchise_id | franchise_name: Official franchise name – derives from team_franchise.franchise_name | active: Active flag (likely boolean or smallint) indicating whether the franchise is active – derives from team_franchise.active | na_assoc: North American association flag (likely boolean or smallint) indicating NA affiliation – derives from team_franchise.na_assoc
params.metric: franchise_id = team_franchise.franchise_id | franchise_name = team_franchise.franchise_name | active = team_franchise.active | na_assoc = team_franchise.na_assoc
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_season_summary on franchise_id — safe because team_franchise is one-row-per-franchise and will not duplicate season-level aggregates when joined on franchise_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on franchise_id only if player_core is pre-aggregated to one-row-per-franchise; otherwise do not join directly (see unsafe guidance below). | do NOT join directly to batting_season_player_agg or pitching_season_player_agg on franchise_id without first aggregating those tables to franchise-level (e.g., SUM or COUNT grouped by franchise_id), because batting_season_player_agg and pitching_season_player_agg are many-rows-per-franchise (player-season granularity) and will multiply this view's rows/measures. | do NOT join directly to player_season_rank_by_hits, player_season_above_threshold_cohort, player_awards_summary, or salary_player_year on franchise_id without aggregating them to one row per franchise_id first, because those sibling views are per-player or per-player-season and are many-to-one relative to franchise. | safe composition pattern: when combining franchise flags with player- or season-level measures, either (a) aggregate the many-side to franchise_id before joining (e.g., SELECT f.*, agg.* FROM team_franchise_active f LEFT JOIN (SELECT franchise_id, SUM(... ) AS metric FROM batting_season_player_agg GROUP BY franchise_id) agg USING (franchise_id)), or (b) keep the result at the more granular grain (player or season) and LEFT JOIN team_franchise_active (one-row-per-franchise) on franchise_id — this preserves the granular cardinality and does not duplicate the franchise flags.

views.description: Active franchises (as identified in team_franchise). Useful for filtering analyses to currently active franchises. Keep specific active flag selection outside the CTE if needed. | Use for: List franchises and filter by active='Y' to limit to current franchises; Join to team to show franchise names for team-season rows

views.name: player_awards_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  COUNT(*) AS awards_count,
  MIN(year) AS first_award_year,
  MAX(year) AS last_award_year
FROM player_award
GROUP BY player_id

params.description: Per-player aggregate summary of awards: total count and the first and last award years for each player.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of awards per player | Filter or rank players by award activity (e.g., players with > N awards) | Enrich player-level profiles with award history (first/last award year) | Compose player-level metrics combining awards with season or salary data (must respect cardinality guidance)
params.output_schema: player_id: unique identifier for a player — derived from player_award.player_id | awards_count: total number of award rows for the player — derived from COUNT(*) over player_award rows | first_award_year: earliest award year for the player — derived from MIN(player_award.year) | last_award_year: latest award year for the player — derived from MAX(player_award.year)
params.metric: awards_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of player_award rows grouped by player_id | first_award_year = MIN(player_award.year)  -- earliest year value among player_award rows for the player | last_award_year = MAX(player_award.year)  -- latest year value among player_award rows for the player
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_id — safe because player_core is one-row-per-player (NORM), so this view's one-row-per-player measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_franchise_active on franchise_id only after joining player_core (or ensure player->franchise is one-to-one for the desired key) — safe if the right-side is one-row-per-key. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to salary_player_year on player_id and year only if you first align years (this view is one-row-per-player, not per-year); joining salary_player_year (which is one-to-many by player across years) directly will multiplicatively duplicate awards_count unless you aggregate salary_player_year to player-level (e.g., SUM/single-year filter) before joining. | DO NOT join directly to batting_season_player_agg or pitching_season_player_agg without re-aggregation: those are per-player-per-season aggregates (one-to-many relative to this view) and will multiply awards_count/other per-player measures. To combine, either (a) aggregate the season-level view to player-level first (e.g., SUM or MAX by player_id) and then join, or (b) join and compute appropriate per-player aggregates in a single grouped query re-aggregating after the join. | DO NOT join directly to player_season_above_threshold_cohort or player_season_rank_by_hits without re-aggregation for the same reason (they are season-level or multi-row per player). Aggregate to one row per player or use analytic approaches that avoid duplicating counts. | Safe composition pattern examples: | - To get awards_count alongside player attributes: SELECT p.*, a.awards_count, a.first_award_year, a.last_award_year FROM player_core p LEFT JOIN player_awards_summary a USING (player_id); | - To compare awards_count to career_salary: first aggregate salary_player_year to player-level (e.g., total_salary_by_player) then join to this view on player_id. | - To compute awards per season: join this view to a player-season aggregate only after reducing that season view to one row per player (e.g., average seasons played) or compute a ratio in a query that re-aggregates properly. | Rationale: player_awards_summary is strictly one-row-per-player (GROUP BY player_id). Joining to any table/view that has many rows per player will duplicate the awards_count and min/max year unless that other side is reduced to one row per player or the query re-aggregates after the join.

views.description: Aggregate count of awards per player across years (from player_award). Useful to identify multi-award winners, join to player for profiles, or filter for award-winning players. | Use for: Find players with multiple awards or award timelines; Join with player to display award counts alongside biographical info

views.name: salary_player_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  team_id,
  league_id,
  player_id,
  salary
FROM salary

params.description: Provides one-row-per-player-per-team-per-year salary records: the salary a player was paid for a given team in a given year (from the salary table).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve a player's salary for a specific year and team | Compare salaries across players within the same year and team | Compose season-level player financial summaries by joining with season player aggregates (must respect join cardinality) | Filter or cohort players by salary when building analytic cohorts | Join to team- or league-level season summaries to analyze payrolls by team or league
params.output_schema: year: calendar or season year for the salary record — derived directly from salary.year | team_id: identifier of the team paying the salary — derived directly from salary.team_id | league_id: identifier of the league the team belonged to that year — derived directly from salary.league_id | player_id: identifier of the player receiving the salary — derived directly from salary.player_id | salary: monetary amount paid to the player for that year/team — derived directly from salary.salary
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_id — safe because player_core is a 1:1 normalized player dimension (one row per player_id), so joining will not duplicate salary rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_franchise_active on team_id AND year — safe if team_franchise_active is modeled as one row per team_id per year (a selector view) because it will not multiply salary rows when joined on those keys. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_season_summary on team_id AND year — safe because team_season_summary is an aggregate at team-season grain (one row per team_id/year); joining will preserve one salary row per player-season and attach team metrics without duplicating salary measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to park_reference on team_id (or park id if available) — safe if park_reference is a normalized lookup with one row per team/park; verify the park key matches to avoid unintended multiplicity. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to batting_season_player_agg or pitching_season_player_agg directly if those aggregates are at the same grain (player_id, team_id, year) is OK — joining on (player_id, team_id, year) is safe because both are one row per player-season-team; however, if those sibling aggregates are at a different grain, you must align keys or re-aggregate first. | do NOT join this view to any one-to-many child detail (for example, a transaction or game-level table with multiple rows per player_id/team_id/year) without first aggregating the child to the salary view's grain (year, team_id, player_id). Joining such a detail directly would multiply the salary rows and thereby duplicate the salary measure. | when composing metrics that sum salary after joining to other tables, ensure the join preserves 1:1 or many:1 from the salary view's perspective. If joining to a table that has multiple rows per (year, team_id, player_id), aggregate that table up to (year, team_id, player_id) before joining, or perform the aggregation after joining using DISTINCT keys to avoid double-counting.

views.description: Player-season salary facts (one row per player-year-team salary record). Useful to join salary to player-season aggregates or team-season to analyze pay vs performance. | Use for: Join salaries to batting_season_player_agg or pitching_season_player_agg to compute pay per performance; Aggregate payroll by team-season

views.name: park_reference
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  park_id,
  park_name,
  park_alias,
  city,
  state,
  country
FROM park

params.description: Provides a normalized reference table of parks (one row per park_id) with basic identifying attributes (name, alias, city, state, country).
params.when_to_use: Look up park metadata by park_id (name, alias, city, state, country). | Annotate aggregated baseball metrics (team, season, player summaries) with park identifying information by park_id. | Filter or group results by park attributes (city/state/country) when building higher-level aggregates — after joining, re-aggregate as needed.
params.output_schema: park_id: Unique identifier for the park — derived from park.park_id | park_name: Official name of the park — derived from park.park_name | park_alias: Alternate or short name for the park — derived from park.park_alias | city: City where the park is located — derived from park.city | state: State/province where the park is located — derived from park.state | country: Country where the park is located — derived from park.country
params.grounded_columns: park.park_id | park.park_name | park.park_alias | park.city | park.state | park.country
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_season_summary on park_id — safe because park_reference is one-row-per-park_id (primary key park_id) so joining team_season_summary (which is many seasons/teams referencing a park_id) will not duplicate park_reference measures; the correct join pattern is team_season_summary.park_id = park_reference.park_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to salary_player_year on park_id is only safe if salary_player_year is at most one row per park_id (it likely is not); do NOT assume safe — instead join salary_player_year to the relevant aggregation (e.g., aggregate salary by park_id first) before combining with park_reference to avoid multiplying rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to pitching_season_player_agg or batting_season_player_agg on park_id is NOT safe without re-aggregation first because those are many-to-one (many player-season rows reference the same park_id) and would multiply counts/metrics from aggregations built on park_reference. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on park_id is NOT safe unless player_core is known to be one-row-per-park_id (it is not); instead join player_core to a derived aggregation keyed by player_id or re-aggregate after joining. | When composing: treat park_reference as a dimension (lookup) with neutral measures. It contains no aggregates/metrics, only attributes, so joining it to many-row fact tables is safe from the perspective of not duplicating pre-computed measures stored in this view — the duplication risk is that the fact side will expand the result set. If you need to preserve aggregations from the fact side, perform joins before aggregation or re-aggregate after joining. | Do NOT join park_reference to any one-to-many table/view and then assume the row-count equals number of parks; always aggregate on the many side (e.g., COUNT(*) BY park_id) if you need park-level measures.

views.description: Canonical park reference useful for attaching park names and location to team-season home parks or home_game records. | Use for: Resolve park names and locations for team-season park analysis; Join with home_game to analyze attendance by park
